sections.h2: Selling in Brownsville at a glance
sections.html:
Brownsville sits on the Rio Grande, facing Matamoros, and serves as the seat of Cameron County. Most sales involve three local offices: the appraisal district, the clerk and the tax office. Population was estimated at 192,957 in mid-2025, 3.6% above the 2020 base. Owners live in about 61.7% of homes. The median home value is $139,900 and the median rent is $923.

Because 83.6% of residents over age five speak another language at home, contracts here are often read in two languages. Everyone on the deed should understand the paper before signing it.

sections.h2: How Cameron CAD sets your value
sections.html:
Value comes from the Cameron Appraisal District, while each taxing unit chooses its own rate. The district reappraises every property at least once every three years, and more often where prices move quickly.

A small increase of $1,000 or less needs no notice of appraised value, which is why some owners never see a mailing. Section 23.23 of the Tax Code, in force since January 1, 2008, holds growth in a homestead's assessed value to 10% a year. New rooms, pools and similar improvements sit outside that cap.

You prove Texas residency with something like a driver's license. Married owners each apply and show ID. Four exemptions cover a residence: homestead, over-65, disabled person and 100% disabled veteran. A disabled veteran exemption may be placed on any single property the veteran owns instead.

  • You can claim over-65 or disabled in a given year, not both.
  • Where only part of the ownership lives in the house, the account is divided and the exemption is scaled to the qualifying owner's percentage.
  • Adding a pool, garage or room raises the school tax ceiling. A Tax Ceiling Transfer form carries it to a new Texas homestead.

A few exemption types need a new application by April 30 each year. Ask the district which ones apply to you.

The protest goes in writing, due on the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice reached you. Mail, hand delivery and email all work. A mailed one needs a postmark by the deadline.

After the deadline, the district and the review board lose the power to change the value. Hospitalization can excuse a late filing. Forgetting cannot. File on time and you receive at least 15 days' notice of a hearing that tends to last about 15 minutes. If the result still looks wrong, the options are district court, binding arbitration or, here in Cameron County, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

  • Name the owner and give the property address or account number.
  • State the issue, such as market value.
  • Attach comparable sales, photos or repair estimates as support.

January 1 fixes both value and the tax lien. Cameron County Tax Office is on East Levee Street, at the same address as the clerk. Call it to learn which taxing units bill your address and what the payoff is.

Key dates for a Brownsville property tax bill
WhenEvent for the owner
January 1Value and the year's lien are set
April 30Some exemption types need a new application
May 15, or day 30 after the noticeLast day to protest, whichever falls later
Around October 1Bills arrive
February 1Balances still owed become delinquent: six percent penalty, one percent interest
After July 1Twelve percent penalty; the taxing unit's lawyer may tack on up to 20 percent

Clear title is impossible with delinquent tax on the books, so pay any balance by closing.

sections.h2: What if the property is headed for a tax sale?
sections.html:
Tax sales are auctions conducted by a constable or a hired agent. No statewide list exists. Look for notices on county websites.

Redemption rights depend on the kind of property. A homestead, farm or mineral owner has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, at a 25% premium in the first year or 50% in the second, plus costs. Anything else has 180 days and a premium of up to 25%. Money left over after the sale belongs to the former owner, who has two years from the sale date to ask for it.

Valley family land often remains titled to a relative who died decades ago. An affidavit of heirship, sworn and filed with the county clerk, is the quick fix, but no judge reviews it and a title insurer may refuse to rely on it.

Sturdier options: open probate within four years; use a muniment of title when the estate's only debts are liens on the real estate; or rely on a transfer on death deed recorded during the owner's lifetime. An heir missing from the recorded deed can still seek an exemption by bringing the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: Where a Brownsville deed is recorded
sections.html:
The Cameron County Clerk, 835 E. Levee Street, holds deeds, liens, plats and maps. After a deed is recorded, bring Cameron CAD the instrument, or its volume and page numbers, so the owner of record gets updated.

Expect $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each following page, plus other fees listed in the state clerk manual. Call the clerk for your deed's total.

Pick the route by looking at the house itself. A tidy home can draw several buyers who need mortgages, but you wait on appraisals and lender calendars. A home with an aging roof, a stubborn tenant or years of unpaid tax suits a buyer who pays cash, accepts the problems and closes once title work clears.

Line up each offer on the same three points: price, closing costs and closing date. Then let the title company confirm that no tax or lien item changes the figure.

Open a folder before you call anyone. Inside, keep the latest county tax bill, the appraisal notice if one came, and the Cameron CAD account number with its exemption list. Loan payoff letter, lease, probate papers or recorded affidavit go in too, whichever apply. Ask the clerk whether liens or old instruments are filed against the property, because a lien found late stalls a closing.

Before funds move, the title company obtains the tax balance, runs a lien search and works out which signatures are needed. It settles any mortgage with the payoff figure. For an inherited house, the probate or affidavit route has to be sorted out first. The deed is then signed, acknowledged and recorded by the county clerk.

Your homestead exemption stays with you, so a buyer who intends to live there applies for a new one. If someone is still in the house, settle a move-out date with the buyer before you sign the contract.

faqs.q: What does a typical Brownsville home cost?
faqs.a: Median value for an owner-occupied home is $139,900, but condition, lot and street move any single sale up or down.

faqs.q: Will Cameron CAD always mail a value notice?
faqs.a: No. A notice goes out only when the law calls for one, and an increase of $1,000 or less needs none.

faqs.q: When is a Brownsville appraisal protest due?
faqs.a: By the later of May 15 and 30 days after delivery of the notice. It must be written, and you may mail it, bring it in or email it.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Brownsville deed?
faqs.a: Go to the county clerk on East Levee Street. The appraisal district does not hand out deeds, surveys or plats.

faqs.q: Does a Brownsville homeowner over 65 get a tax ceiling?
faqs.a: Yes. School taxes on the home usually stay flat for as long as you own and live in it, and the ceiling can follow you to a new Texas homestead.
